findings.text: the path head "section_declarations" is restated here and in the startswith literal, duplicating DECLARATIONS_PATH_HEAD at reckon/_store_section_ops.py:76 which the store's own dispatch keys on; a rename of that head would silently detach the readiness fields from the landing write that leaves a plan closable, and no test would redden because the same literal appears on both the string compared and the fixture that writes it.

the documented failure path — readiness null with readiness_error naming why, the write still succeeding — is asserted by nothing in tests/test_a_finishing_write_offers_its_close.py, so a regression that lets the roadmap read escape after the completed write, or drops the readiness_error key, passes every gate the node ran.

the negative-control log carries a bare Terminated line above the pytest output that no run record attributes; the red arm is still readable (FF., 2 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1) and matches the fragment's quote, but an unattributable kill message in a gate log is exactly the line a later reader cannot tell from one that ended the run.
